newsitem.title: DUBAI: Japan-Gulf Arab trade hits $37.5 billion in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Japan-Gulf Arab trade hits $37.5 billion in 1996.

text.p: Trade between Japan and Gulf Arab states climbed by 11.8 percent in 1996 to $37.5 billion, the highest level since 1984, official figures showed on Saturday.
The Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) said trade between Japan and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states rose from $33.6 billion in 1995.
"In 1996, a much weakened yen boosted Japanese exports to the GCC countries and a high oil price also swelled the Japanese import bill from the GCC countries," JETRO said in a statement.

Japan boosted its exports to the Gulf Arab states by 11.5 percent in 1996, selling motor vehicles, general machinery, electrical machinery and others goods worth $7.3 billion, compared to $6.5 billion in 1995.
GCC states -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Oman and the United Arab Emirates -- sold $30.3 billion in goods to Japan in 1996, up from $27.1 billion in 1995.
The UAE was the leading Gulf Arab exporter to Japan in 1996, followed by Saudi Arabia.
Japan imported $23 billion in crude oil from Gulf Arab states in 1996 compared to $20.2 billion in the previous year.
Japan imported about 70 percent of its crude oil from Gulf Arab states, JETRO said.
